meta.paper: Krapp LF, Abriata LA, Cortes Rodriguez F, Dal Peraro M. PeSTo: parameter-free geometric deep learning for accurate prediction of protein binding interfaces. Nature Communications 14:2175 (2023).
meta.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (authors code and weights); this reproduction and its scripts carry the same licence; non-commercial use
meta.hardware: CPU only, 4 threads (OMP/MKL/torch), nice 19, no GPU
meta.pipeline: E:/Ciencia/PIPELINE.md, padrao meio-termo com pre-registro; this file is hashed with SHA-256 before any dataset is built or any model weight is loaded

fixed_definitions.model: model/save/i_v4_1_2021-09-07_11-21/model_ckpt.pt, config_model from the same folder (32 geometric transformers, element-only features)
fixed_definitions.features: features_flags = (True, False, False), i.e. one-hot atomic element only (30 channels), as in the authors data_handler.Dataset default
fixed_definitions.topology: 64 nearest neighbours per atom (extract_topology(X, 64)); batch of one structure packed with collate_batch_features so that index 0 is the sink node
fixed_definitions.prediction: sigmoid of the model output, column 0 (protein-protein interface), one value per residue
fixed_definitions.label: a residue of the target subunit is positive iff it has a residue-residue contact within 5.0 A with any atom of another subunit whose residue names are in categ_to_resnames[protein] (the r_types[0] column of the authors label construction). Computed by me from the bioassembly, not read from the authors files
fixed_definitions.metric: sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score per structure, on residue-level label vs residue-level prediction
fixed_definitions.aggregate: numpy.median over structures; a structure whose label has no positive or no negative residue is dropped from the median (same rule as the authors roc_auc in src/scoring.py, which returns NaN there)
fixed_definitions.dataset_build: my own reimplementation of processing/build_dataset.py: read the legacy RCSB biological-assembly PDB file (files.rcsb.org/pub/pdb/data/biounit/PDB/divided/xx/pdbid.pdbN.gz) with gemmi, chain name tagged with the model index, drop the assembly if the raw atom count (before any cleaning, waters and hydrogens included) is >= 8192, then clean_structure (drop water/H/D), tag_hetatm_chains, split_by_chain, filter_non_atomic_subunits, require >= 2 subunits, remove_duplicate_tagged_subunits, and keep a subunit only if it has at least one 5 A contact with another subunit
fixed_definitions.masif_set: start from the 53 names in masif-site_benchmark/testing_transient.txt; keep only names that have a per-residue MaSIF-site prediction in masif-site_benchmark/masif_pred_per_res.json (51 names); build every bioassembly of those PDB entries; keep every subunit entry whose sid (PDBID_chain) is in those 51 names AND whose residue count equals the length of the MaSIF-site per-residue prediction for that sid. The residue-count filter is the authors own filter in interface_ppi_benchmark.ipynb. The count of entries obtained is itself a claim (C5)
fixed_definitions.scannet_set: the 417 sids listed in column A of sheet Fig2b-ScanNet of the Source Data file (41467_2023_37701_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx). The bioassembly and model tag of each are NOT published, so: use bioassembly 1; among the subunit entries of assembly 1 whose sid matches, take the one with the lowest model tag; if assembly 1 yields no entry for that sid, try assemblies 2,3,... in order and take the first that does, and report how many sids needed that fallback
fixed_definitions.scannet_sampling_fallback: if a timing measurement on 10 structures implies more than 6 h of wall clock for the full 417, run a random sample instead: numpy.random.default_rng(20261108).choice(417, 150, replace=False), and report the sample median together with its bootstrap 95 percent interval
fixed_definitions.ambiguity_rule: any definition not fixed here that turns out to matter is reported as an extra analysis and does not change the verdict

claims.text: Median ROC AUC of PeSTo on the MaSIF-site benchmark subunits
claims.where: Fig. 2b and main text (PeSTo reaches a median ROC AUC of 0.92 against 0.8 for MaSIF-site)
claims.tolerance: abs(mine - 0.92) <= 0.03, AND mine inside the bootstrap 95 percent interval of the median of the authors own per-structure values, [0.891, 0.948] (20000 resamples, seed 0, computed from sheet Fig2b-comparison before this file was hashed)

claims.text: Median ROC AUC of PeSTo on the set of structures shared with the ScanNet benchmark
claims.where: Fig. 2b and main text (a benchmark dataset of 417 structures commonly shared by the two methods ... a median ROC AUC of 0.93 against 0.87)
claims.tolerance: abs(mine - 0.93) <= 0.02, AND mine inside the bootstrap 95 percent interval of the median of the authors own per-structure values, [0.909, 0.940]
claims.cost: 417 CPU inferences (or the pre-registered sample of 150)

claims.text: PeSTo has a higher ROC AUC than every other method benchmarked on the MaSIF-site set for 38 of 53 structures
claims.where: main text (higher ROC AUC than all other methods benchmarked here for 38 out of 53 structures)
claims.tolerance: abs(mine - 38) <= 3. Computed with MY PeSTo AUC against the authors published per-structure AUCs for MaSIF-site, SPPIDER and PSIVER (sheet Fig2b-comparison), because the SPPIDER and PSIVER per-residue predictions are not in the repository

claims.text: Median ROC AUC of MaSIF-site on the same 53 structures
claims.tolerance: abs(mine - 0.80) <= 0.03. Computed from the authors released per-residue MaSIF-site predictions (masif_pred_per_res.json) scored against MY labels. This is a check of my label reconstruction, not of MaSIF-site

claims.text: The MaSIF-site benchmark set, as defined by the paper and the authors code, contains 53 subunit entries
claims.where: main text (38 out of 53 structures), Methods (the 53 subunits from the MaSIF-site benchmark dataset)
claims.tolerance: exact: my set must have 53 entries and the same multiset of sids as column A of sheet Fig2b-comparison of the Source Data. Any difference is reported structure by structure

what_counts_as_reproduced: C1, C2, C3 inside tolerance -> Reproduced. One of them outside -> Partially reproduced, with the cause investigated (todays PDB files vs 2023s, the 8192-atom limit, choice of bioassembly, my own bug). C5 failing does not by itself break the verdict but is reported.
